correctness.rationale: Exact reduction: inversion on positions i<j occurs iff no cut intersects [i,j-1]. Shattered t-interval supports have distinct private cut positions, which force maximum incidence at most 2 for any point and t<=2r. At t=2r, private/zero-incidence/double-incidence witnesses are disjoint and require at least 4r chain positions; independent four-position gadgets attain equality. For two cuts, private/zero/double counting gives exact thresholds m=3,4,6,8 for VC sizes 1..4, with explicit supports. A complete eight-leaf adaptive tree proves first gap at m=5; hypothesis counts prove optimality and earlier equality. Independent blockwise threshold trees and counting prove the logarithmic asymptotic. Both executable checkers passed, but finite computation is not used as proof of asymptotic claims.

value.rationale: The 4r point threshold is a sharp all-parameter static shattering phase boundary for a standard permutation subclass, not a mere fixed-instance enumeration. The all-length three-layer classification and explicit first adaptive gap clarify what extra power adaptive comparisons gain. For every fixed number of layers the proven r log n growth yields an unbounded gap while static dimension remains bounded; this is a structural learning-theoretic distinction with exact finite thresholds and reproducible certificates.
